Which statement about the speed and velocity of an object is correct?
A
The speed and velocity of an object are always greater than zero.
B
The speed of an object is always greater than its velocity.
C
The velocity of an object is equal to its speed in a given direction.
D
Speed can be measured in m/s but velocity can only be measured in km/h.

options.label: A
options.text: The speed and velocity of an object are always greater than zero.

options.label: B
options.text: The speed of an object is always greater than its velocity.

options.label: C
options.text: The velocity of an object is equal to its speed in a given direction.

options.label: D
options.text: Speed can be measured in m/s but velocity can only be measured in km/h.
